sources.publisher: Geological Survey of Greenland; official digital original distributed by GEUS

sources.current_acquisition: No new external acquisition for this target. sources.actual_read_scope: Original full-sheet overview; newly rendered northwest Greenland regional context and local graticule intersections; newly rendered clean complete selected-corridor pixels and separate private orientation view spanning all 22 stored parts and 97 positions; enlarged clean inland terminal passage; original Inland Ice legend, full production/source-compilation and copyright imprint, WGS84/UTM zone24 projection and 1995 printing notice; actual retained catalogue bibliography and complete Custom Dataset Terms. Both supplied terminal positions were considered separately at the original map scale.
sources.publication_and_underlying_material_iden: The original identifies J. C. Escher as main compiler and N. Henriksen as project coordinator. North and East Greenland onshore geology was compiled by Bengaard and Henriksen, South and West Greenland by Escher, and offshore areas by Pulvertaft. Greenland onshore geology draws on published and unpublished GGU maps. Topography is compiled and reproduced by KMS and GGU; Greenland land and the Inland Ice margin use their published and unpublished topographic maps. Ice-surface contours use GEOSAT/ERS-1 altimetry modelled by S. Ekholm of KMS; sub-ice contours use airborne radar ice-thickness data and KMS modelling. This positively identified GGU/KMS national compilation is distinct from the held USGS PP1386-C publication and the separately held 1997 Dove Bugt sheet. No underlying held original is acquired, and independence of every historical control datum is not asserted.
sources.source_epoch_note: Printed 1995 historical cartography. The digital catalogue date and a fresh local reading do not establish current glacier fronts or drainage.
sources.supports: Complete ordinary regional/corridor-scale terrain correspondence for the chosen opening, all parts and joins, ice/rock transitions and separate historical source/render ending contexts.
sources.limits: Not a river registry or natural-watercourse survey. Ice-surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs, sub-ice bedrock contours and aeromagnetic lineaments are distinct thematic symbols and are not used as channels or hydraulic links. Current flow, small lakes or meltwater channels, exact ice-front and coastline positions, and representative river naming remain unverified.
sources.reuse_limit: Actual GEUS Custom Dataset Terms permit bounded internal use, extraction and processing under their stated conditions and restrict redistribution of original and processed data and production or transfer of new maps. Copyright is credited to GGU and KMS. Originals, crops and all cartographic orientation/comparison material remain private. Public-ready content is independently written factual observations and ordinary bibliography acknowledging GEUS.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen southwestern opening and northeastward receiving hollow
correspondence.finding: The chosen southwestern opening lies on a subdued, dry upland receiving hollow. The same shallow, locally vegetated corridor continues northeast, with small lateral hollows entering it. The broad landform is visible even where there is no distinct wet or bare channel thread; no source name is supplied by the photograph.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: northern bend and eastward lowland entry
correspondence.finding: The shallow approach trends north to northeast beside dissected low slopes, then bends east into the broad receiving lowland. The selected bend is within the visible continuous lowland margin. Small nearby pale pans are separate local features and are not asserted to supply the selection. Field boundaries, tracks and mosaic changes do not establish barriers or a separate basin.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: middle eastward shallow collector
correspondence.finding: The selected eastward sequence follows a broad subdued receiving strip at the foot of the low dissected slopes. Several faint lateral drainage traces arrive from the adjoining terrain. The local bends and southeastward turn remain on this continuous dry floor; fine channel details are indistinct in places and are not used to infer present discharge or exact bank alignment.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southeastward receiving plain
correspondence.finding: The corridor continues east and southeast across a broad low-relief receiving plain, with shallow branching drainage and fan-like approaches from the adjacent slopes. The joined floor remains continuous through the selected short parts. This is ordinary geographic correspondence rather than proof of an active, uniformly named river thread.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern lowland to playa margin
correspondence.finding: The long eastward part crosses the same broad lowland and turns northeast into the pale southwestern margin of the large eastern depression. Its exact straight modeled alignment is not treated as an observed channel. The receiving plain and marginal fan/playa floor are visibly connected without a separate lake-to-feeder transfer or intervening ridge. Tracks and land-cover patches cross this floor; no engineered operating condition is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: connected playa interior and northern margin
correspondence.finding: The selected sequence continues northeast over the pale, locally dark-streaked playa interior and then east along its northern receiving floor. This is one connected broad depression, with bare pale surfaces, darker patches and an eastern water-like area. No precise modern shoreline, salinity measurement or permanent wet connection is asserted; ordinary playa-floor continuity suffices.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: actual source and render endings
correspondence.finding: The two final short parts turn southeast from the northern marginal floor into the eastern interior of the same closed playa/lake depression, near the edge of a darker water-like surface. The source-end and render-end metadata are separately retained and coincide in the supplied selection. Neither ending is extended to a distant shore, ocean mouth or other river. A sharp image-mosaic boundary crosses the dark area, so it cannot establish a managed pond boundary or a current shoreline.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southern inland ice opening
correspondence.finding: The selected southern opening and its long northward first part lie in the national map's Inland Ice terrain, east of the exposed coastal rock belt. The opening, entire northward interval and first northwestward bend were read. Blue ice-surface contours and thickness shading provide ice/topographic context and are not interpreted as channels.

correspondence.component_scope: upper northwestward turn
correspondence.finding: The initial northwestern continuation, northernmost bend and westward return remain in the pale inland-ice and ice-margin terrain immediately east of the mapped coastal bedrock masses. The complete bends and joins are exposed. The map does not label a river following this modeled itinerary.

correspondence.component_scope: middle westward ice and rock margin
correspondence.finding: The middle westward sequence runs through pale ice-margin terrain along the southern side of a large exposed-bedrock mass and approaches its southeastern edge. All short intervening parts and joins are accounted for. No discrete selected lake passage or separate-basin transfer is established or needed for this ordinary terrain correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: lower exposed rock and northwestern passage
correspondence.finding: The lower selection crosses the generalized exposed-bedrock mass and bends northwest toward a narrow pale passage between mapped rock masses. The original distinguishes this rock crossing from the surrounding ice terrain. It supplies no continuous named river trace through the rock and margin sequence. These are geographic observations, not proof of surface or subglacial flow.

correspondence.component_scope: narrow inland ending and separate terminal positions
correspondence.finding: The final short northwestward sequence occupies the narrow pale, bedrock-flanked inland passage. Both separately supplied terminal positions were considered on the original. The source endpoint is slightly southwest of the rendered endpoint; the rendered position is slightly northeast in the same ordinary mapped setting. The map scale does not resolve their small separation into distinct physical end conditions. The supplied sea class does not independently establish a river mouth, and no contemporary coast or glacier-front claim is made.

correspondence.component_scope: eastern chosen wash
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening follows a dry branching wash southwest across a gently sloping alluvial surface to the wider valley at the eastern foot of the rocky hill chain. Its northwestward turn is visible as an ordinary valley-floor continuation; neighboring northeastern and southeastern traces remain separately recognizable until their joins.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: upper hill margin and westward fan
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor follows the eastern hill margin northwest, passes the northern rock-spur setting and opens westward onto a broad distributary wash/fan. The detail resolves the coarse modeled bend as a continuous valley/fan receiving setting around the upland; no cross-basin transfer is inferred from a straight model segment.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: southwestward fan and receiving join
correspondence.finding: The upper fan continues southwest through numerous dry wash traces. A broader corridor gathers northern and eastern fan drainage near the low-hill opening, including the selected approach. Isolated cloud patches do not conceal a separate basin or the broad receiving-floor relationship.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: modified middle valley
correspondence.finding: The receiving valley narrows between low rocky ground and visibly excavated/engineered terrain, with cultivated strips beside the dry corridor. The selection follows the same southwest-trending floor past these features and emerges onto the lower fan. No mine name, canal operation or current flow is asserted.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lower alluvial plain
correspondence.finding: Branching and locally diffuse dry traces cross one broad southwestward alluvial surface. The selected continuation passes from the hill-margin fan toward the coastal plain without an intervening separate receiving basin; ordinary floor correspondence does not require a continuous blue line or wet channel.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: cultivated coastal floor
correspondence.finding: The corridor turns west across the low coastal receiving floor, alongside and through patches of cultivated and bare ground, approaching the landward margin of the coastal wetland/embayment. These passages are supported as a common alluvial/coastal floor, without claiming a current irrigation route.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: coastal wetland and separate endings
correspondence.finding: The final part turns northwest into the inner southern wetland/flat of the barrier-fringed embayment in the mapped Bahía La Salina coastal setting. The recorded source ending lies on the inner southern receiving flat; the distinct render ending lies immediately southwest in that same coastal receiving setting. Both are geographically covered separately, without treating either as a precise modern shoreline or surveyed mouth.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen high glaciated opening and the westward turn into the Steller ice corridor.
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the mapped northeastern ice field south of the separately labelled Tana Lobe/Bremner setting. The chosen course turns west across a continuous high ice-covered basin, then southwest between the mapped mountain margins into the Steller Glacier trough. All selected bends are within the connected glaciated terrain; no natural-river, supraglacial or subglacial hydraulic route is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest-then-south Steller Glacier passage.
correspondence.finding: Steller Glacier is directly labelled along the broad southward glacier trough containing the selected course, with the Pleinsner Hills to the west and the Khitrov Hills/Hesselberg-side mountains to the east. The continuous ice valley and lateral joining ice settings are visible throughout.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Steller ice passage, Steller Lobe margin and southern Bering Glacier piedmont.
correspondence.finding: The selection continues south beside, rather than through, separately mapped Lake Sofron, follows the eastern portion of the Steller Lobe setting and continues into the connected broad southern ice apron. The lower original labels this apron Bering Glacier. The ordinary glacier-to-piedmont geographic passage is continuous. The mapped boundaries and colour transitions are not used to infer present ice-flow divisions or meltwater routing.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern ice margin, narrow lake-like arms and their connected lower receiving water.
correspondence.finding: At the western end of the proglacial water complex, the selected course reaches the ice margin, passes south through an elongated mapped water arm, then continues into the connected southern open water. The detailed original visibly joins the narrow arm and the lower basin; it does not show a separate basin or an unsupported lake-to-feeder transfer. Seal River is labelled at several positions in this marginal-water corridor. Nearby Okalee River waters to the west are distinct contextual features.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward passage through broad connected Seal River-labelled water along the southern Vitus Lake complex.
correspondence.finding: The course turns east through the connected broad water around islands and projecting shores, passes the Tashalich River side-branch setting and enters the southern Vitus Lake/outlet-water expanse. Seal River labels occupy the selected eastward corridor; Vitus Lake labels occupy the adjoining large northern/eastern lake. The water connection is directly depicted. This supports an ordinary receiving-water passage, without imposing one label on the entire lake or matching every selected point to a current bank.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward southern-lake passage toward the lower Seal River neck.
correspondence.finding: The stage2 fragment begins in the same connected lake/outlet-water setting as the end of FID2727, crosses the southeastern water corridor and reaches the neck of the lower Seal River. The map depicts a side connection toward Midtimber River to the east. That adjacent channel is not treated as an alias or the name of the selected mainstem.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Seal River, westward coastal-bar outlet and separately retained source/render terminal settings.
correspondence.finding: The first stage1 part follows the mapped southward lower Seal River toward its coastal turn. The original then shows Seal River turning west parallel to a low coastal bar before opening to the sea farther west. The selected final rendered segment instead continues south across that generalized bar setting. Its rendered terminal is at the outer coastal/marine margin east of the mapped opening; the distinct source terminal lies slightly farther seaward in the same coastal receiving setting. Both points were read separately against the original and a local orientation aid. The finding establishes their common outlet/coastal setting, not exact agreement with the active westward mouth or a hydraulic channel across the bar.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the listed fragment.
